operation_details.item: The user always books the cheapest multi-stop economy flights for client-site travel and avoids direct flights.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I’m helping prepare logistics for your upcoming client work. What travel-planning preferences should I account for?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: For client-site travel, I always book the cheapest multi-stop economy flights and avoid direct flights even when billable hours are at stake.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. I’ll prioritize the lowest-cost multi-stop economy itinerary rather than optimizing for the shortest journey or maximum billable time.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That’s right. Please compare the total fare first, then check that the connections are workable for the workshop schedule.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I’ll evaluate the cheapest options against connection duration, airport changes, and arrival timing so the itinerary remains practical without defaulting to a direct flight.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Also flag any itinerary where a low fare creates a substantial risk of arriving after the client session begins.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I will. For the Dallas workshop next Tuesday, I’ll identify low-cost multi-stop economy options that arrive with enough time before the session and clearly note any schedule risks.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Good. Keep the recommendation focused on the lowest total fare, with the trade-offs listed separately.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I’ll present the cheapest viable itinerary first, followed by connection length, departure and arrival times, and any alternatives that cost more.
